hlni.insight: Academic tasks are defined by their assessment criteria, not the degree title.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree names imply specific, uniform teaching or grading methods.
hlni.viewerChange: Students shift from guessing degree value to asking institutions about concrete evaluation rubrics.
hlni.support: The method isolates three variables—product, criterion, and feedback—to expose missing information before committing to a choice.
hlni.payoff: The student identifies the '?' placeholders in their audit, turning abstract degree confusion into a precise, actionable question for admissions.

candidate.creativeAngle: Using a tripartite question method to audit academic tasks instead of relying on degree labels.
candidate.objective: Teach students how to evaluate B.Com and BBA curricula by focusing on assessment criteria rather than generic titles.
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Comparison Trap
shots.visual: A student looks at two folders labelled 'B.Com' and 'BBA' with a frustrated expression.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA based on names alone misses the most important part: how you are actually assessed.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on student, then pans to the folders.

shots.name: The Assessment Audit
shots.visual: Student holds a sheet with three columns: Product, Graded on, Feedback. They write 'Floor Plan' in the first column.
shots.dialogue: Use this audit. Take a sample task and map it. Example: Task: Floor Plan | Graded on: ? | Feedback: ?
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Floor Plan | Graded on: ? | Feedback: ?
shots.cameraPerformance: Over-the-shoulder shot showing the pen filling the worksheet.

shots.name: The Concrete Question
shots.visual: Student circles the question marks and looks directly at the camera.
shots.dialogue: The blanks are your guide. Now you know exactly what to ask: What specific criteria do you use to grade this project?
shots.onscreenText: What specific criteria do you use to grade this project?
shots.cameraPerformance: Direct address to camera, confident tone.

productionNotes.camera: Stable, tripod-mounted, clear focus on the worksheet.
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts synchronized with the writing steps.
productionNotes.sound: Ambient room tone with clear, crisp voiceover.
props: Two folders labelled B.Com and BBA

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the comparison from degree prestige to specific assessment methods using a tripartite worksheet.

selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a degree's name reveals the grading criteria.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Learns to ask about evaluation methods instead of relying on degree labels.
selected.concept: A student maps out three columns for a potential task: Product, Criterion, Feedback.
selected.device: Split-screen comparison of a blank worksheet being filled out while narrating the need for specific criteria.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: A hypothetical task: 'Develop a shop floor plan'.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Floor Plan | Graded on: ? | Feedback: ?
demonstration.observation: The student realizes they have a task but zero information on what counts as 'good' or how they learn.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific criteria do you use to grade this project?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of a blank worksheet being filled out while narrating the need for specific criteria.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: Natural, informal conversation between two peers using a shared notebook.

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A quick-fire quiz where the 'correct' answer is that there isn't enough info.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / tripartite_question_mapping; Connection = task_question_journal / recorded_sticking_point; Discovery = insufficient_information / forced_choice_refutation. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

qa.failureReason: fidelity: The hook introduces B.Com and BBA as the comparison subjects, but these subjects are entirely abandoned in the second and third shots, which focus exclusively on a generic floor plan task. Revision: Ensure the student evaluates a specific task related to either B.Com or BBA in the second shot to maintain the integrity of the initial comparison. insight: The student identifies that they have zero information on how they learn or what counts as good, but the transition from the worksheet to the final question is abrupt and lacks the student recording the specific sticking point as required by the 'task-question journal' method. Revision: Include a brief moment of the student vocalizing the observation of the missing information before transitioning to the final question to demonstrate the intended HLNI process.
